items.title: Ann Rabson interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, September 21, 2007
items.q: And my mom was, you know, she was really busy and stuff.

ctx.x: I’ll be. That’s a neat coincidence. Were you able to go to — who could you go to in your family, or whatever, and you’re four years old and like try to share this feeling?

My father. Absolutely. My father was so excited that I was excited about music. He went out and got records and showed me — he could play boogie woogie and showed me some of that, and definitely. I mean my brother and I were not on real good terms much in my childhood. And my mom was, you know, she was really busy and stuff. But my dad, he was really the one who encouraged me, and is still encouraging me.
That’s great. Was there a point when you were a teenager or whatever, that you really decided I want to be a professional musician?
